components.text: Supply a valid, sound, evidentially supported demonstration before accepting God-belief.
Whether evidential argument can use logic without first accounting for logic under the critic’s worldview.
Show why inability to prove ultimate reality prevents any justified truth-directed inquiry.
Whether failure to defeat hard solipsism prevents all practical knowledge and truth-directed inquiry.
Establish that a godless worldview cannot account for logical absolutes or rational cognition.
Whether identifying difficulty for naturalism demonstrates that Christianity uniquely accounts for logical absolutes.
Whether merely assigning suitable qualities to God actually explains logical necessity.
Explain why differing perceptions or lack of ultimate access makes truth or knowledge unavailable.
Whether differing internal perceptions prevent objective truth or knowledge of an external reality.
Whether individual cognitive outputs exhaust the objective standards used to assess them.
Establish reasonable God-belief rather than assume God's existence as the reason for itself.
Whether presupposing God’s truth can itself establish that God-belief is reasonable.
Justify relying on reason and experience while acknowledging no ultimate solution to skepticism.
Whether generally reliable experience can justify reliance on sense and reason without vicious circularity.
Provide an adequately supported valid and sound demonstration of God rather than assume the claim.
Apply the same shared evidential standard to God that is applied to other disputed propositions.
Whether God must be established by independent evidence before evidence can rationally support God-belief.
Whether the evidential demand can be applied from a neutral framework rather than a God-grounded one.
Explain how future-directed reasoning can be warranted without infallibly proving cognitive reliability.
Whether induction must provide certainty about future conformity in order to rationally support predictions.
Justify using past observations as a rational basis for future probabilistic predictions.
Whether looking back at successful reasoning can justify using past patterns to predict future events.
Show that the affirmative uniquely accounts for logical absolutes rather than only challenging the opponent's account.
Whether inability by an opponent to provide an ultimate account establishes the asserted Christian account.
Whether Christianity’s claimed account of logical absolutes has itself been demonstrated.
Provide a method for distinguishing Christianity from incompatible rival purported revelations.
Address divisions within Christianity and establish a generally reliable revelation discriminator.
Whether a competing religious revelation can be discriminated from Christianity by an internal-consistency test.
Whether the proposed method reliably distinguishes the wider set of religions and Christian denominations.
Assess the specific Quran-Bible premises and whether they internally refute the rival revelation.
Demonstrate that revelation reliably supplies knowledge of the claimed divine grounding.
Whether the Quranic premises and alleged contradiction actually establish an internal refutation of Islam.
Whether alleged revelation supplies an independently demonstrated mechanism for knowing the claimed truths.
Explain how intrachristian disagreement affects identification of a reliable specifically Christian revelation.
Provide a verifiable method for deciding among incompatible religious and denominational claims.
Independently demonstrate the truth or revelatory mechanism of the identified essential claims.
Whether internal Christian disagreement defeats identification of a shared specifically Christian revelation.
Whether a reliable method distinguishes Christianity from other incompatible religious revelations.
Whether the listed essential claims and their revelatory source are independently demonstrated.
